problem_statement: The paper frames several finance tasks as targets for hybrid quantum-classical machine learning: modelling financial distributions for cryptocurrency data, predicting stock prices from time series, and generating synthetic market data. It also presents option pricing and portfolio-related optimization as part of the finance motivation.
problem_statement_quotes: In this work, we explore emerging research areas in the application of hybrid classical quantum machine learning (QML) in finance.

This paper focuses on novel implementation of the following QML algorithms as applied to financial industry: a) application of quantum-classical hybrid Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (qGAN) treated with new data leveraging authors’ previous work [49], b) a hybrid classical-quantum Quantum Long Short Memory (QLSTM) for stock prediction using real-life stock price data of NVIDIA and c) Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) motivated by [5] leveraging authors’ previous work [49],
In this paper we explore the implementation of a qGAN for the uncertainty model on option pricing using real world data from Binance.
A hybrid quantum-classical model was implemented, inspired by Chen et al. [35], for stock price prediction using QLSTM.
Originally, reliable synthetic market modelling was done through sampling from parametric models that can be easily calibrated.
classical_baseline: For the stock-prediction part, the paper compares QLSTM against a classical LSTM model. For the generative-modelling part, it contrasts qGANs with classical GANs, and for synthetic market modelling it references parametric classical models such as multivariate normal distributions and Gaussian copulas.
classical_baseline_quotes: comparing its performance with classical Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) model.

Originally, reliable synthetic market modelling was done through sampling from parametric models that can be easily calibrated. Examples are multivariate normal distribution of risk factor equities or a Gaussian copula.
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical Monte Carlo for portfolio loss distribution is expensive computationally and time-wise because it requires many samples and trajectories. It also says stock prediction is challenging because of the non-linear and volatile nature of the market, and that classical GANs can suffer from instability, vanishing gradients, and mode collapse.
